title: A task commit carries what the index says and the verdict it was measured under
desiredOutcome: commit-task-work commits both halves of a staged rename or deletion, stages a tracked file under an ignored directory and leaves the index as found on any refusal, names an untracked ignored file instead of passing silently, and refuses a task whose newest gate verdict is not passed on the work being committed unless the operator overrides it on the record

findings.issue: verdict_binding hands the raw task.files list to _tree_stamp.scope_digest, which hashes each entry with _journal_io.file_hash(project/entry). An entry with a ':line-range' suffix, or a directory entry, hashes as None ('missing') at gate time AND at commit time, so field_state answers AGREES whatever happened to the file. Probed: owns=['src/a.py:10-20'] and owns=['src'], changing src/a.py -> 'agree

--record takes the scopeDigest inside run_gate, then write_pointer writes task.testEvidence into the phase file (the manifest itself in the single-file layout) and write_evidence_since also writes the manifest. A task declaring its own manifest/phase file is always MOVED and refused; re-running the gate rewrites the pointer again, so --override-verdict is the only way out.

The empty-gate check returns no-gate before the ledger is read: a task with a newest FAILED row whose gates are later emptied commits without an override, and the NO_GATE sentence says the recorder 'writes no verdict for it' while a red one sits in the ledger. Separately the row's gate is never compared with the gate declared now: a passed row measured under an older/narrower tests.gate still bind

4c's exit-1 remedy for a foreign staged path is 'declare them with /audit:task scope'. Widening task.files changes the set scope_digest hashes, so the next commit is refused as MOVED with 'the declared files have changed since it was measured' - untrue when only the list changed. The doc does not say a scope change after the gate forces a re-measure.

Branches with no case: _in_head's unborn-HEAD arm; index_snapshot's write-tree refusal (unmerged index); INDEX_NOT_RESTORED; override_row failing after the commit (exit 1 with the SHA); the unreadable-ledger refusal; a reused row whose source is missing; the UNANSWERABLE and NOT_DECLARED arms; '--override-verdict was given and not needed'.

'which gate measures a task is now one function, _manifest_io.gate_entries()' is untrue: copies remain in _panel_composition._gate_source (its docstring's reason - the rule lives in an L7 entry point it may not import - is now stale), _report_html.py:548 (counts all-blank entries as a gate), gen-demo-manifest.py:1727 (no fallback from an all-blank task gate), _manifest_phases._gate_entries.

--no-renames in the shared foreign_staged also changes what commit-audit-state and commit-manifest-index refuse (a staged rename from outside their allow-list into it now names and refuses its source). A fix, but the CHANGELOG credits commit-task-work only and no case pins it for the other two.

Docs say the index is restored 'exactly as it was found', but write-tree drops intent-to-add entries (' A ita' becomes '?? ita') and refuses an index with unmerged entries, so a conflict resolved in the tree but not added - which plain git add used to resolve - is now refused. Neither refusal is in the documented exit-1 causes.

'ignored' also takes the record paths (phase file, journal, evidence) when git ignores them, and the refusal advises 'drop it from the task's files', wrong for a record path. A declared file untracked with git rm --cached and then ignored also gets '-f is yours to decide' when the operator wants the deletion committed.
One unreadable line in any ledger file refuses every task commit in the project, and names no repair.

tasks.title: commit-task-work commits a staged rename's source, stages tracked files under ignored directories, and is bound to the task's newest verdict
tasks.description: Field report on 3.0.1, reproduced at HEAD: (1) tracked() asks the index only; after git mv the old path is only in HEAD, so the red-first skip drops it and the commit records a copy. Tracked = index OR HEAD; a HEAD-only path stays out of the git add argv (git add -- old fails 128) and in the git commit -- pathspec (records the rename). Cases for a staged R and a staged D. (2) git add -- <tracked file under an ignored dir> exits 1 AND stages it (git 2.50.1); the script refuses and leaves it staged, breaking 'a refusal leaves the index as found'. Split by ls-files: tracked -> git add -u --, untracked -> git add --; the ignore refusal survives only for untracked paths, named 'ignored; -f is yours to decide'; any failure after staging resets the allowed paths; an untracked declared file under an ignored dir is named, not 'nothing uncommitted'. Never add -f. (3) the commit ignores task.testEvidence: refuse unless the task's newest evidence row is passed and current for the staged work (the declared-work digest run-test-gate records matches what is staged); an explicit override flag writes a journal row. No runtime related-tests step.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_commit_task_work.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a declared path staged as the source of a rename is skipped, so the commit adds the new file and leaves the old one tracked

outcome.technical: Paths only in HEAD stay in the commit pathspec; add -u for index entries with the index restored on failure; the newest evidence row must be passed with a matching declared-work digest, --override-verdict journals the exception.
outcome.descriptive: A task commit records renames and deletions, stages tracked files under ignored directories, and refuses work whose newest gate verdict is not passed.

tasks.title: Sign-off review findings: the verdict digest covers suffixed and directory entries and skips record paths, an emptied or changed gate is still graded, and all three scoped commits stage and restore alike
tasks.description:
Findings of the phase review, every one to be fixed (or answered with a measured reason) in this task:
R1 (high) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/commit-task-work.py (verdict_binding) with plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_tree_stamp.py (scope_digest): verdict_binding hands the raw task.files list to _tree_stamp.scope_digest, which hashes each entry with _journal_io.file_hash(project/entry). An entry with a ':line-range' suffix, or a directory entry, hashes as None ('missing') at gate time AND at commit time, so field_state answers AGREES whatever happened to the file. Probed: owns=['src/a.py:10-20'] and owns=['src'], changing src/a.py -> 'agrees', basis '1 declared file(s); 0 read, 1 missing'. The command then prints that the digest matches, which is false. -> Normalise the scope ONCE in _tree_stamp and use it on both sides (run-test-gate's tested_state and commit-task-work): strip the line suffix (_vocab._strip_line_suffix), expand a directory into the files git lists under it; or refuse UNANSWERABLE when an entry that exists on disk hashed None. Cases for a suffixed entry and a directory entry edited after a green gate, red first.
R2 (med) commit-task-work.py verdict_binding; run-test-gate.py _record_run -> _evidence_io.write_pointer: --record takes the scopeDigest inside run_gate, then write_pointer writes task.testEvidence into the phase file (the manifest itself in the single-file layout) and write_evidence_since also writes the manifest. A task declaring its own manifest/phase file is always MOVED and refused; re-running the gate rewrites the pointer again, so --override-verdict is the only way out. -> Leave the plugin's own record paths (the phase file / manifest, evidence and journal dirs) out of the scope digest on both sides, as reuse_identity already does for the content identity; or digest that file with the pointer block removed. Case: a single-file-layout task that declares audit-plan.json.
R3 (med) commit-task-work.py verdict_binding (the 'if not entries' early return): The empty-gate check returns no-gate before the ledger is read: a task with a newest FAILED row whose gates are later emptied commits without an override, and the NO_GATE sentence says the recorder 'writes no verdict for it' while a red one sits in the ledger. Separately the row's gate is never compared with the gate declared now: a passed row measured under an older/narrower tests.gate still binds after the gate is widened. -> Read the task's rows before deciding no-gate; a newest row is graded (or at least named). Compare the row's gate (step names / declared_gate over current entries) with gate_entries now and refuse on mismatch. Cases: red-then-emptied, gate-changed-after-green.
R4 (med) plugins/audit/reference/execute-task.md step 4c; commit-task-work.py: 4c's exit-1 remedy for a foreign staged path is 'declare them with /audit:task scope'. Widening task.files changes the set scope_digest hashes, so the next commit is refused as MOVED with 'the declared files have changed since it was measured' - untrue when only the list changed. The doc does not say a scope change after the gate forces a re-measure. -> Tell a list change from a content change (record the declared scope in testedState or derive it from scopeBasis) and word each refusal; add to 4c that widening scope after the gate means recording the gate again.
R5 (med) plugins/audit/tests/test_commit_task_work.py: Branches with no case: _in_head's unborn-HEAD arm; index_snapshot's write-tree refusal (unmerged index); INDEX_NOT_RESTORED; override_row failing after the commit (exit 1 with the SHA); the unreadable-ledger refusal; a reused row whose source is missing; the UNANSWERABLE and NOT_DECLARED arms; '--override-verdict was given and not needed'. -> One case per branch, each fixture telling its branch apart from its neighbours; prove each red by mutating the branch.
R6 (low) CHANGELOG.md: 'which gate measures a task is now one function, _manifest_io.gate_entries()' is untrue: copies remain in _panel_composition._gate_source (its docstring's reason - the rule lives in an L7 entry point it may not import - is now stale), _report_html.py:548 (counts all-blank entries as a gate), gen-demo-manifest.py:1727 (no fallback from an all-blank task gate), _manifest_phases._gate_entries. -> Move those copies onto _manifest_io.gate_entries (fix across all surfaces) and keep the CHANGELOG sentence true.
R7 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_scoped_commit.py foreign_staged; CHANGELOG.md: --no-renames in the shared foreign_staged also changes what commit-audit-state and commit-manifest-index refuse (a staged rename from outside their allow-list into it now names and refuses its source). A fix, but the CHANGELOG credits commit-task-work only and no case pins it for the other two. -> CHANGELOG line for the other two; one case each in test_commit_audit_state and test_commit_manifest_index.
R8 (low) commit-task-work.py index_snapshot/restore_index; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md; execute-task.md: Docs say the index is restored 'exactly as it was found', but write-tree drops intent-to-add entries (' A ita' becomes '?? ita') and refuses an index with unmerged entries, so a conflict resolved in the tree but not added - which plain git add used to resolve - is now refused. Neither refusal is in the documented exit-1 causes. -> Snapshot with ls-files -s + update-index --index-info so flags survive (or qualify the sentence); list the unmerged-index refusal under exit 1.
R9 (low) commit-task-work.py stage_targets / ignored_refusal: 'ignored' also takes the record paths (phase file, journal, evidence) when git ignores them, and the refusal advises 'drop it from the task's files', wrong for a record path. A declared file untracked with git rm --cached and then ignored also gets '-f is yours to decide' when the operator wants the deletion committed. -> Word the record-path refusal separately; recognise in-HEAD + absent-from-index + ignored as a deletion to commit.
R10 (low) commit-task-work.py (unreadable-ledger refusal): One unreadable line in any ledger file refuses every task commit in the project, and names no repair. -> Name the file holding the torn line and the command that shows it; or narrow to lines that could carry this task's id.
pre-existing 1 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/commit-audit-state.py; commit-manifest-index.py: Both still stage with one git add -- allowed and do not restore the index on any failure after staging; commit-audit-state's git commit has no pathspec. The defects fixed in commit-task-work, open in the other two scoped commits. -> Move index_snapshot, restore_index and the per-kind staging into _scoped_commit, have all three use them, restore cases in each suite.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_commit_task_work.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a task declaring src/a.py:10-20 commits after src/a.py changed since its green gate

outcome.technical: _tree_stamp.declared_scope normalises suffixes and directories, record paths excluded, scopeListDigest recorded; _scoped_commit.stage_and_commit shared with pathspec commits and ls-files/update-index restore; one gate normaliser.
outcome.descriptive: A task commit can no longer pass on work that changed since its gate, and the three scoped commits stage and restore the index the same way.
